क्या AI कभी सिनेमा में इंसानी हुनर और एक्टिंग की जगह ले पाएगा? 🎬

फिल्म Ramayana के VFX और इसकी भव्य दुनिया को लेकर सोशल मीडिया पर काफी बहस छिड़ी हुई है। हाल ही में BBC News से बातचीत में Ranbir Kapoor और Yash ने AI के इस्तेमाल पर अपनी बेबाक राय साझा की। Ranbir Kapoor का मानना है कि AI सिर्फ एक टूल की तरह काम कर सकता है, लेकिन यह इंसानी टच और आर्ट को कभी रिप्लेस नहीं कर सकता। 🤖

वहीं Yash ने कहा कि इंसान हर सिचुएशन में सरवाइव कर लेता है और हमें इस टेक्नोलॉजी को बहुत सावधानी से इस्तेमाल करने की जरूरत है। इसके साथ ही IIMUN इवेंट में फिल्म के VFX और म्यूजिक की ट्रोलिंग पर जवाब देते हुए Ranbir Kapoor ने कहा कि "कुछ तो लोग कहेंगे, लोगों का काम है कहना"। उन्हें ट्रोलिंग से कोई फर्क नहीं पड़ता क्योंकि उनकी नीयत साफ है। 😎

Nitesh Tiwari के डायरेक्शन और Namit Malhotra के प्रोडक्शन में बन रही इस ग्रैंड फिल्म में Ranbir Kapoor (Lord Rama), Sai Pallavi (Sita) और Yash (Ravana) के किरदार में दिखेंगे। फिल्म का पहला पार्ट 5 November 2026 और दूसरा पार्ट Diwali 2027 के आसपास सिनेमाघरों में आएगा। 📅

क्या आपको लगता है कि फिल्मों में AI कभी कलाकारों के इंसानी टच की जगह ले पाएगा? कमेंट्स में अपनी राय जरूर दें! 👇

ctx.title: Ranbir Kapoor weighs in on AI's impact on filmmaking, says it can never replace human touch
ctx.summary: While promoting Ramayana, Ranbir Kapoor and Yash said AI can support filmmaking but cannot replace human creativity and performance.
ctx.text:
Ranbir Kapoor and Yash are currently busy promoting their much-awaited film, Ramayana . Since the release of its teaser, the film's VFX and grand world-building have been topics of discussion, with fans weighing in on both its positive and negative aspects. Amid the debate, Ranbir and Yash recently discussed the use of AI in filmmaking and shared why they believe that while the technology can aid the process, it can never replace the performing arts.
Speaking to BBC News about the impact of AI on films, Ranbir said, "Art is always more personal when there is a human touch to it. I think AI like VFX or camera lenses, can be used as a tool to better your filmmaking. But from the medium we come from – of storytelling, of art, of performing art -- and I don’t think AI can ever replace that."
Yash also weighed in on the debate and said, "We have to be responsible enough to understand that humans are involved in it, and we need to be very cautious in where all we apply this technology. We are survivors. We will come up with some idea or we will create something which even a machine would have to struggle with."
In another interaction, Ranbir addressed the criticism that Ramayana has been receiving over aspects such as its VFX and music. Speaking at an India International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN) event, Ranbir admitted that he remains unbothered by the criticism because his intentions are clear.
Ranbir said, “What's relevant today is this beauty of trolling online. It goes back to the good old song ‘Kuchh to log kahenge, logon ka kaam hai kehna (People will say something, it's their job to say something or the other)'. I think that's a great philosophy to actually follow in life. Don't be bothered by what people are saying. What matters is the people who matter, the people who care for your work, your intention, and your kindness. That's what matters the most."
Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is a two-part adaptation of the Indian epic, produced by Namit Malhotra. Ranbir plays Lord Rama, while Sai Pallavi essays the role of Sita and Yash plays Ravana. The first part is scheduled to release in cinemas worldwide on November 5, 2026, while the second might release around Diwali 2027.

She began her career covering Delhi's cultural scene, food, nightlife, concerts, and city life at The Times of India, before moving into full-time entertainment journalism with India Today.

At India Today, Vibha interviewed some of the biggest names in Bollywood and television while carving a niche for herself through film reviews, opinion pieces, nostalgic features, celebrity interviews, and trend-driven stories. She later brought her storytelling and editorial expertise to The Indian Express, where she continued to deepen her understanding of cinema through long-form entertainment explainers, retrospectives and feature writing.
